texts.preamble: Mohd Naveed Baghwan, vs The State Of Telangana, on 6 April, 2023 Author: Abhinand Kumar Shavili Bench: Abhinand Kumar Shavili The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Abhinand Kumar Shavili And The Hon'Ble Sri Justice Pulla Karthik Writ Petition No.807 Of 2023 Order:
texts.arguments: 2. Heard Ms. R. Sowmya Reddy, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri S. Mujib Kumar, learned Special Government Pleader, representing the learned Additional Advocate General appearing for the respondents. 3. Learned counsel for the petitioner had contended that the brother of the petitioner i.e. detenu was detained by the respondents under the provisions of the Act 1 of 1986 vide impugned detention order, dated 24.12.2022, on the alleged ground that he was involved in Crime No.137 of 2022 of Lingala Ghanpur Police Station, Warangal Police Commissionerate, registered for the offence under Section 8(c) read with 20(b)(ii)(C) of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances Act, 1985. Learned counsel for the petitioner further contended that the issue whether the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 can be invoked based upon a solitary crime or not, was considered by a Division Bench of this Court in W.P.No.30726 of 2022, dated 23.09.2022, wherein this Court has [LEAKAGE_MASK] the detention order impugned therein with an observation that the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 cannot be 3 AKS,J & PK,J invoked based upon a solitary crime. Admittedly, in the instant case also, the detaining authority has invoked the provisions under the Act 1 of 1986 against the detenu based Mohd Naveed Baghwan, vs The State Of Telangana, on 6 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/32374251/ 1 upon a solitary crime registered against him. Therefore, appropriate orders be passed in the Writ Petition by setting aside the impugned orders and set free the detenu immediately. 4. On the other hand, the learned Special Government Pleader appearing for the respondents had contended that huge quantity of ganja was seized from the detenu.
